Sean / team,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We're narrowing in on a pilot (care routing assistant) that will be latency-sensitive for short queries (user prompts ~25-80 tokens) and occasionally long transcripts (~1k tokens) for post-call summarization. A few asks so procurement and infra can align:

- Can you provide a rough tokens/sec and tokens/sec-per-GPU estimate for the model variant we saw (gptx-l6-quant)?
- We need SLO recommendations (p95 latency targets) and recommended headroom for safe bursts during rollout.
- Any idea on how many reserved GPUs we'd need for a 50k daily active users projection (typical burst window 9–11am PT, peak concurrent sessions estimate ~800)?

I've attached the usage sketch and expected QPS distribution. Procurement (Christine) is copied — we'll need the rough numbers to scope procurement language and costs.

Alex — thanks for the clear sketch. Quick high-level responses and assumptions below; Marcus added the detailed calc in a follow-up.

Assumptions (short):
- Model: gptx-l6-quant (avg token cost per response ~0.9 tokens generated per input token, KV cache for multi-turn)
- Typical short query path: 25–80 tokens total (we'll assume avg 45 tokens generated per request)
- Long transcript job: 1,000 tokens (batched, can be scheduled off-peak if you prefer lower cost)
- Target SLO: p95 <= 250ms for short queries (interactive UX), p95 <= 2s for long transcript background jobs.

Preliminary throughput numbers (ballpark):
- Single A100-80GB equivalent (quantized profile) sustained: ~1200–1600 tokens/sec for short-turn inference (lower latency path, continuous batching disabled to keep p95 under 250ms).
- With aggressive batching (background), same GPU: ~6k–8k tokens/sec for batched transcript processing.

Headroom guidance:
- For interactive path keep 30–40% headroom above expected peak to avoid p95 regressions during traffic spikes and retries.

Estimate for ZenHealth pilot (based on your peak concurrent ~800 sessions, avg short-turn latency target):
- If each live session issues 0.8 request/min during the 9–11am window -> ~640 req/min -> ~10.7 req/sec.
- At avg 45 tokens generated, that's ~480 tokens/sec across system.
- With p95 target and low batching, 1 A100-equivalent can handle ~1500 tokens/sec comfortably -> 1 GPU gives ~3x headroom.

Recommendation: start with 1–2 reserved GPUs for the interactive path (1 primary, 1 reserved/failover + can be used for low-priority batching outside peak). For transcript batch jobs, consider a separate 1 GPU pool (can be preemptible/dedicated depending on SLA).

I'm attaching a quick notes file with the calc. Happy to sync with procurement and engineering tomorrow.

—Sean

Adding the engineering breakdown and the conservative assumptions we should surface to procurement: 

Detailed assumptions and calc (conservative):
- Short interactive request: 45 generated tokens avg, ~15 input tokens avg -> total tokens processed ~60 tokens per request (includes KV lookups).
- Measured tokens/sec per A100-80 (quant profile) under low-latency mode: 1,400 tokens/sec (p50 latency 60–80ms, p95 ~220–260ms depending on sequence length). Use 1,400 as baseline.
- Peak concurrency mapping: 800 concurrent sessions -> assume 0.013 requests/sec/session (0.8 req/min) -> ~10.4 rps -> 10.4 * 60 tokens = ~624 tokens/sec.
- Safety margin: 2.5x headroom recommended for first 6–8 weeks (traffic patterns and retries) -> target capacity ~1,560 tokens/sec.
- GPUs required (interactive): ceil(1,560 / 1,400) = 2 GPUs reserved. One can be configured as active+standby with scheduled warm-up.
- For transcript batch (1k tokens each) at 100 jobs/hour during peak -> 100k tokens/hour -> ~27.8 tokens/sec average; batched throughput on same A100 opportunistically ~7k tokens/sec -> single GPU sufficient for batch footprint (non-interactive).

Operational notes:
- Autoscale policy: keep a 1-GPU buffer in the pool during peak (free to be used for short bursts), scale to 3 GPUs if weekly peak exceeds 2x projected baseline for 2 consecutive days.
- Fallbacks: route to hosted model variant (slower quant) if dedicated pool saturated — this preserves availability but may increase latency.

I'll drop a small spreadsheet with per-minute QPS -> GPU mapping. If procurement needs a conservative number for the SOW, quote 2 reserved GPUs for interactive with the option to add 1 more within 30 days.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infra Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
